This project aimed to enhance climate resilience in Georgetown City, with a focus on flood-hazard mitigation. By strategically employing "Suitability" and "Urban Performance" Urban Planning Tools developed by CAPSUS, the initiative supported evidence-based decision-making processes to guide sustainable urban development. Key activities included a comprehensive assessment of the potential social and economic impacts of flood hazards on the population, built-up areas, critical amenities, and urban infrastructure. The project also raised awareness among key stakeholders about the value of digital tools and spatial insights for prioritizing interventions, reducing vulnerability, and fostering long-term resilience to climate risks.
